```{r setup, include = FALSE}
source("_setup.R")
library(bayesmokken)
```

```{r fits, include = FALSE}
data(classroom_wb)
items <- paste0("wb", 1:6)
sup <- bm_supports(classroom_wb, items = items)
f_resp  <- bm_cached("cwb_respondent")
f_equal <- bm_cached("cwb_equal_cluster")
iv_r <- bm_interval(f_resp)
iv_e <- bm_interval(f_equal)
info <- bm_cluster_info(classroom_wb$class_id, data = classroom_wb[, items])
```

When respondents are nested in clusters, two things must be settled that were
never in question before: **which** population quantity is being estimated, and
**how** uncertainty is generated. This vignette does both.

## Two estimands, not one estimand and one nuisance

At the population level, let $M$ be cluster size and $F$ a cluster's response
distribution. The respondent target is the size-weighted mixture
$F_{\mathrm{resp}}=E(MF)/E(M)$; the equal-cluster target is
$F_{\mathrm{eq}}=E(F)$. The former corresponds to sampling a respondent
uniformly. The latter corresponds to sampling a cluster uniformly and then a
respondent uniformly within that cluster.

In a finite sample, write $g = 1, \dots, G$ for clusters and $n_g$ for the size
of cluster $g$, so $n = \sum_g n_g$. The plug-in coefficients use cluster
weights

$$H_{\text{resp}} : \ \omega_g = \frac{n_g}{n},
\qquad\qquad
H_{\text{eq}} : \ \omega_g = \frac{1}{G} .$$

These are sample plug-ins for the two population mixtures, not definitions of
those population distributions. Under equal cluster sizes the plug-ins
coincide. Under **informative cluster size** — when $n_g$ is associated with
the response distribution — they need not.

```{r informative}
data.frame(
  clusters          = info$G,
  respondents       = info$N,
  smallest_cluster  = min(info$sizes),
  largest_cluster   = max(info$sizes),
  informative_index = round(info$informative_index, 3)
)
```

```{r fig-clusters, fig.alt = "Classrooms ordered by size with the weight each target assigns to each: respondent weighting increases with class size while equal-cluster weighting stays flat."}
bm_plot_clusters(classroom_wb$class_id, show_targets = TRUE)
```

```{r targets-differ}
c(respondent = iv_r$point_estimate, equal_cluster = iv_e$point_estimate,
  difference = iv_r$point_estimate - iv_e$point_estimate)
```

That difference is
`r fmt_h(abs(iv_r$point_estimate - iv_e$point_estimate), 4)` here. It is not
sampling error and it does not shrink with $n$. Because neither is more correct
than the other, `cluster_target` has no default, and omitting it is an error
rather than a silent choice.

```{r no-default, error = TRUE}
bb_mokken_h(classroom_wb[, items], item_type = "ordinal", supports = sup,
            cluster = as.character(classroom_wb$class_id),
            weight_law = "hierarchical_cluster", draws = 200, seed = 1)
```

## The two-stage hierarchical bootstrap

Uncertainty enters at both levels at which sampling happened. Independently per
draw,

$$(u_1, \dots, u_G) \sim \mathrm{Dirichlet}(1_G),
\qquad
(v_{g1}, \dots, v_{g n_g}) \sim \mathrm{Dirichlet}(1_{n_g}) \ \text{ for each } g,$$

and the respondent weight is then assembled to match the chosen target:

$$w_{gi}^{\text{resp}} \ \propto\ \frac{n_g}{n} \, u_g \, v_{gi},
\qquad\qquad
w_{gi}^{\text{eq}} \ \propto\ \frac{1}{G} \, u_g \, v_{gi} .$$

The upper stage carries between-cluster variability; the lower stage carries
within-cluster variability; the target enters only through the fixed factor.
That factor is what makes each draw an estimate of *its own* estimand rather
than of a common one.

### Independent oracle: the seeded HBB weight law

```{r verify-weights}
cluster <- as.character(classroom_wb$class_id)
cluster_info <- bayesmokken:::bm_validate_cluster(cluster)
sizes <- cluster_info$sizes
G <- cluster_info$G
n <- cluster_info$N

# Independent reconstruction of the locked RNG law. This does not call the
# package's Dirichlet or weight helpers.
oracle_hbb <- function(cluster, draws, seed, target) {
  label <- as.character(cluster)
  lev <- unique(label)
  index <- match(label, lev)
  size <- tabulate(index, nbins = length(lev))
  old_kind <- RNGkind()
  had_seed <- exists(".Random.seed", envir = .GlobalEnv, inherits = FALSE)
  old_seed <- if (had_seed) get(".Random.seed", envir = .GlobalEnv) else NULL
  on.exit({
    do.call(RNGkind, as.list(old_kind))
    if (had_seed) {
      assign(".Random.seed", old_seed, envir = .GlobalEnv)
    } else if (exists(".Random.seed", envir = .GlobalEnv, inherits = FALSE)) {
      rm(".Random.seed", envir = .GlobalEnv)
    }
  }, add = TRUE)
  RNGkind("L'Ecuyer-CMRG")
  set.seed(seed)
  draw_simplex <- function(k) {
    out <- matrix(stats::rexp(k * draws), nrow = k, ncol = draws)
    sweep(out, 2, colSums(out), "/")
  }
  a <- draw_simplex(length(lev))
  out <- matrix(0, length(cluster), draws)
  denominator <- if (target == "respondent") colSums(size * a) else rep(1, draws)
  for (g in seq_along(lev)) {
    rows <- which(index == g)
    b <- draw_simplex(length(rows))
    multiplier <- if (target == "respondent") {
      size[g] * a[g, ] / denominator
    } else {
      a[g, ]
    }
    out[rows, ] <- sweep(b, 2, multiplier, "*")
  }
  out
}

hbb_resp <- bayesmokken:::bm_cluster_hbb_weights(
  cluster_info, draws = 8, seed = 18022, target = "respondent"
)
hbb_eq <- bayesmokken:::bm_cluster_hbb_weights(
  cluster_info, draws = 8, seed = 18022, target = "equal_cluster"
)
oracle_resp <- oracle_hbb(cluster, 8, 18022, "respondent")
oracle_eq <- oracle_hbb(cluster, 8, 18022, "equal_cluster")

stopifnot(
  identical(hbb_resp$weights, oracle_resp),
  identical(hbb_eq$weights, oracle_eq),
  all(abs(colSums(hbb_resp$weights) - 1) < 1e-14),
  all(abs(colSums(hbb_eq$weights) - 1) < 1e-14),
  all(hbb_resp$weights >= 0), all(hbb_eq$weights >= 0)
)
c(respondents = n, draws_checked = ncol(hbb_resp$weights), targets_checked = 2)
```

The point targets are recovered by a **mean-vector substitution**: replace
every Dirichlet vector by its mean and then apply the same normalization. This
is not a statement about the expected value of a ratio. In particular,
$E\{n_gA_g/\sum_h n_hA_h\}$ generally differs from
$n_g/\sum_h n_h$.

### Metamorphic/invariant check: mean substitution recovers point weights

```{r verify-cluster-mass}
idx <- rep(seq_len(G), sizes)
mean_a <- rep(1 / G, G)
mean_b <- lapply(sizes, function(size) rep(1 / size, size))

mean_sub_resp <- unlist(Map(
  function(g, b) sizes[g] * mean_a[g] * b,
  seq_len(G), mean_b
))
mean_sub_resp <- mean_sub_resp / sum(mean_sub_resp)
mean_sub_eq <- unlist(Map(
  function(g, b) mean_a[g] * b,
  seq_len(G), mean_b
))
mean_sub_eq <- mean_sub_eq / sum(mean_sub_eq)

point_resp <- bayesmokken:::bm_cluster_point_weights(
  cluster_info, "respondent"
)
point_eq <- bayesmokken:::bm_cluster_point_weights(
  cluster_info, "equal_cluster"
)
stopifnot(
  max(abs(unname(mean_sub_resp) - point_resp)) < 1e-14,
  max(abs(unname(mean_sub_eq) - point_eq)) < 1e-14
)

point_mass_resp <- tapply(point_resp, idx, sum)
point_mass_eq <- tapply(point_eq, idx, sum)
draw_mass_resp <- tapply(hbb_resp$weights[, 1], idx, sum)
draw_mass_eq <- tapply(hbb_eq$weights[, 1], idx, sum)

data.frame(
  size            = sizes,
  point_respondent = round(as.numeric(point_mass_resp), 4),
  point_equal      = round(as.numeric(point_mass_eq), 4),
  one_draw_respondent = round(as.numeric(draw_mass_resp), 4),
  one_draw_equal      = round(as.numeric(draw_mass_eq), 4)
)[order(sizes)[c(1, 2, G - 1, G)], ]
```

The first two mass columns are the finite-sample plug-in targets and are also
what mean-vector substitution recovers. The last two columns are one random
HBB draw, included only to show that realized bootstrap masses fluctuate. No
claim is made that their draw-wise average equals the plug-in target.

## The correction runs the other way

For the binary path the uncorrected interval was too narrow. Here it is too
**wide**: the raw hierarchical interval overcovers substantially, at
$.992$–$.997$ across the pilot's primary-target lanes. So the correction is a
shrinkage,

$$\kappa_G = 1 - \frac{1.5}{\sqrt{G}},$$

which depends on the number of **clusters**, not the number of respondents.
That is the right variable: it is the upper stage, with only $G$ units, that
drives the excess.

**Executable consistency check — reconstruct the adjusted endpoints from the
stored raw interval and observed $G$.**

```{r verify-shrinkage}
kappa_G <- 1 - 1.5 / sqrt(iv_r$cluster_count)
m <- (iv_r$raw_lower + iv_r$raw_upper) / 2
w <- (iv_r$raw_upper - iv_r$raw_lower) / 2

stopifnot(
  all.equal(kappa_G, iv_r$width_multiplier, tolerance = 1e-12),
  all.equal(m - kappa_G * w, iv_r$lower, tolerance = 0),
  all.equal(m + kappa_G * w, iv_r$upper, tolerance = 0)
)
data.frame(G = iv_r$cluster_count, kappa_G = kappa_G,
           binary_kappa_for_comparison = 1 + 0.25 / sqrt(iv_r$n_complete))
```

The two corrections sit either side of 1, and that is not an inconsistency: they
repair opposite defects in two different procedures.

```{r fig-calibration, fig.alt = "Clustered width multiplier versus cluster count: solid from 22 through 80 where confirmation was conducted, dashed outside that range to mark extrapolation, and increasing toward one."}
bm_plot_calibration(mode = "clustered")
```

### $G$ matters, and the validation status is explicit

```{r kappa-table}
data.frame(G = c(22, 30, 50, 80),
           kappa = round(1 - 1.5 / sqrt(c(22, 30, 50, 80)), 4))
```

At $G = 22$ the interval is cut to about 68% of its raw length. A correction
that aggressive has to be earned, and it was confirmed on a grid running from
22 to 80 clusters. Below 22 the calibrated route refuses. From 22 through 80
it reports `CONFIRMED_CLUSTER_COUNT`. Above 80 it returns a result with a typed
warning and `EXTRAPOLATED_CLUSTER_COUNT`; that result is not covered by the
confirmation claim.

```{r range-refusal, error = TRUE}
small <- classroom_wb[classroom_wb$class_id %in% levels(classroom_wb$class_id)[1:10], ]
bb_mokken_h(small[, items], item_type = "ordinal", supports = sup,
            cluster = as.character(droplevels(small$class_id)),
            cluster_target = "respondent", weight_law = "hierarchical_cluster",
            draws = 300, seed = 1, interval = "calibrated")
```

```{r validated-range}
c(status = iv_r$validation_status,
  validated_min = 22, validated_max = 80, this_fit = iv_r$cluster_count)
```

## Guard rails

Three combinations are refused outright, because each would apply a procedure
outside the conditions under which it was confirmed.

**Dichotomous items with a cluster argument.** The clustered method was
developed and confirmed on polytomous items. Refused on every route, including
the uncorrected comparator:

```{r guard-binary, error = TRUE}
data(srs)
bb_mokken_h(srs, cluster = rep(1:25, length.out = nrow(srs)),
            cluster_target = "respondent", draws = 200, seed = 1)
```

**Polytomous items under the independent-respondent law.** Random weights with
no clusters to resample at the upper stage:

```{r guard-iid, error = TRUE}
bb_mokken_h(classroom_wb[, items], item_type = "ordinal", supports = sup,
            weight_law = "iid_respondent", draws = 200, seed = 1)
```

**Undeclared supports.** Shown in `vignette("m1-foundations")`; the denominator
would be computed at a support the user never declared.

```{r guardrails}
bm_guardrails()[1:4, c("situation", "what_to_do")]
```

## The evidence

A fresh 24-cell confirmation crossed 22–80 clusters, intraclass correlations of
$.06$–$.38$, informative-size mechanisms, and transport-path stress lanes.

| Method | Coverage | Length |
|---|---|---|
| **Calibrated (default)** | **.974**, both targets, on the 16-cell regular decision lane | 75% of raw |
| Naive independence BB | .915 | — |
| Two-level delta | .981 | 7% greater |
| Raw hierarchical (uncorrected) | .992–.997 in the pilot | — |

The calibrated interval passed all seven prespecified gates. Applied without
retuning to the SWMDK school data (639 pupils in 30 classrooms), it produces
the intervals shown in `vignette("a3-clustered-polytomous-workflow")`.

The naive independence bootstrap is the instructive comparison. It is what you
get by ignoring the clustering, and at .915 it misses the nominal level by
enough to matter — which is the practical reason this path exists at all.
